assessments.summary: The argument establishes a sound-and-complete Boolean encoding for exactly the stated rct4 subclass. Off both diagonals, cells decompose into disjoint four-cell rho-orbits; with the anti-diagonal empty, the remaining main-diagonal cells decompose into 38 antipodal pairs. Selecting exactly 38 four-orbits and one diagonal pair yields 154 points and precisely the subclass conditions, while every 154-point member uniquely determines such a selection. Because the represented cell sets are disjoint, each maximal lattice-line inequality equals the number of selected points on that line, so the inequalities are equivalent to the no-three-in-line condition.
scopeQualifications: The theorem does not establish satisfiability or infeasibility of the encoding.
It makes no assertion about implementation-specific constraint counts or digests.
It makes no assertion about larger symmetry classes, rotation classification, or the value of D(77).

The report's phrase “every Boolean assignment” is valid only when read as every assignment satisfying the encoding's cardinality requirements; the declared claim itself correctly refers to satisfying assignments.
